queue.what: Every notice this panel emits is swallowed at its own published address. workspace-router.jsx:152 renders CampaignsPage without a notify prop, so ClientsWorkspace falls back to its no-op default. Measured before my fix: a refused offer produced a 400 with a bilingual detail, the form closed, and polling the whole document every 100 ms for 2.5 s found no refusal text anywhere. I mitigated inside my own row with an inline alert, but the product's own toast and its persistent activity feed still record nothing for any pacing write, including the successful ones.

The API and the surface disagree about when a make-good may be raised. POST /api/make-goods on CMP_D040 returns 201 with deficit_kind to_date and deficit_value 0.6, while remedyFor offers that raise on 0 of 56 rows because the flight has unsourced days ahead. The contract defends the surface's rule and it is the better one, but two rules for one act means any other client, Kai included, can put a debt in the ledger the product says is not owed. Either the surface offers the to_date raise with its ladder named, or makegood_store refuses it.

The make-good half of the piece is unreachable from the screen on the shipped data. 0 of 56 rows reach remedyFor kind raise, so the raise control, the offer form and every state after it are exercised by tests and by curl and never by a person. This is correct behaviour on this data rather than a defect, and it means the ledger cannot be assessed against Stripe on real traffic until a flight has every remaining day sourced.

The ledger records no reason on any transition and confirms nothing. Stripe requires a reason on every refund and requires a note when the reason is Other, and confirms a cancellation with 'Yes, cancel refund'. Here 'Withdraw it' and 'Revoke the decision' fire on one click, take an optional free-text note and no reason, and cannot be undone. A withdrawn decision is unauditable.

GET /api/pacing is 184,610 bytes for 56 rows with no windowing on the row list, and grows as campaigns times flight days. It is 17.2 to 24.4 ms warm today, so it is a shape to watch rather than a cost to pay now.

The counted figure is the planned break rating the traffic log carries, not a measured delivery, and the sentence that says so sits behind a collapsed 'How this is counted' disclosure. The row's own word is 'counted' and never 'delivered', which is careful, but a reader who never opens the disclosure can take an at-risk verdict as a measured delivery shortfall. The delivery ledger's own figures_basis says it plainly and is not rendered anywhere on this surface.

21 display strings are split across two source lines by adjacent-literal concatenation, which design-rules.md section 5 now bans. Measured repo-wide the same pattern appears 365 times across 33 kairos_api modules and none of the results contains a newline, so it is a codebase convention rather than a P11 novelty. Needs a lead ruling on whether the rule reaches implicit concatenation before anyone rewrites one module of 33.

The panel's two view controls and its Read again control wrap to a second line at 1440 px, below the heading rather than on its row: measured, the first tab at y=263 and the other two at y=299. The contract says they ride the heading row. It costs 36 px of the fold and the fold count is unchanged at 2 rows, so it is cosmetic.

The delivery ledger's counted_as_of_basis and figures_basis columns are English-only, so a Hebrew reader meets English on asking. This surface handles it correctly, quoting the sentence with lang=en behind the disclosure and attributing it to the ledger, but the underlying columns are P4's and are still monolingual.

closed_this_round: The ledger rendered payload.make_goods, so every recorded acceptance was invisible while the view tab counted it. Measured live: 1 record, 1 in the badge, 0 rows and the empty state on screen. Now renders payload.decisions, the joined timeline, with a kind chip on each row.

actWord(state, kind, locale) was called with two arguments, so kind received the locale and locale was undefined. Every act button printed English to a Hebrew reader and the acceptance verbs were never reachable. Measured after: the acceptance row's control reads בטלו את ההחלטה.

A wrong number on every row. isolate() is a left-to-right isolate and was wrapped around amount(), a phrase that is already Hebrew, so the headline figure of all 56 rows rendered as 4.4 מתוך נקודות רייטינג 35 with the unit ahead of its own number. amount() now isolates its numeral only; six call sites stopped double-wrapping.

pacing-helpers.js imported ../../vocabulary with no extension. Vite resolves that and node does not, and tests/test_p11_surface_remedy.py executes this module in node so its assertions are about the shipped file. All six of those tests failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Every other importer in the product already wrote the extension.

Nine CSS classes the killed round-two run referenced had no rule anywhere: pacing-accept, pacing-accepted, pacing-basis-details, pacing-basis-line, pacing-board, pacing-chrome, pacing-day-weekday, pacing-remedy-book, pacing-remedy-days. The repo build never parses this tree, so they would have shipped unstyled and silent. A guard now compares every class the JSX names against every rule the sheets define.

The behind verdict chip and the declined state chip were --red on --red-soft, measured 4.29:1 against the 4.5:1 AA floor at 11 px. A piece may not define a token and there is no --red-ink, so the pair is inverted: --surface on --red measures 5.09:1, confirmed live in the browser as rgb(194,65,65) on rgb(255,255,255).
The keyboard legend advertised r on a board where 0 of 56 rows can reach a raise. It now names only the keys that fire on the rows in front of the reader, and reads j and k, Enter, a on this data.

The panel rendered an h1 inside a destination that already carries one, above a second stacked view strip. It is an h2 now with its two view controls on the heading row, which took the first row from y=531 to y=441 in an 851 px viewport and put three rows above the fold instead of two.
